fl-duval-2026-atlantic-beach-mayor-s1-fo.name: Curtis R. Ford
fl-duval-2026-atlantic-beach-mayor-s1-fo.bio: Mayor of Atlantic Beach, retired mortgage lender, and former president and CEO of Beaches Habitat for Humanity.

positions.stance: Emphasizes "Smart Planning & Fiscal Responsibility" to make smart decisions and protect taxpayer dollars.
Emphasizes "Transparent Government & Community Trust" through accessible leadership built on honesty and communication.
Emphasizes "Public Safety & Quality of Life" for a safe, beautiful, and vibrant Atlantic Beach.

fl-hillsborough-2026-school-board-d6-gay.name: Kenneth "Ken" Gay
fl-hillsborough-2026-school-board-d6-gay.bio: Retired educator who spent 39 years in Hillsborough County Public Schools as a teacher, instructional leader, and assistant principal.

positions.stance: Focuses on improving academic performance and preparing students for life after graduation.
Says teachers and staff "should have what they need to succeed in the classroom."
Says schools "should maintain discipline and create a positive culture for students and teachers."
Calls for efficient and transparent use of funds and prioritizing money directly to student learning.

fl-hillsborough-2026-school-board-d6-per.name: Karen Perez
fl-hillsborough-2026-school-board-d6-per.bio: Hillsborough County School Board member at-large since 2018, licensed social worker, and president and CEO of Embracing Changes for Wellness, LLC.

positions.stance: Holds the administration accountable and works "to ensure our limited resources make it to the classroom."
Has fought to make the first budget-shortfall cuts at the administration level rather than among teachers and support staff.
Opposes waste "such as overpriced software and bloating of the top executive payroll."

fl-orange-2026-county-mayor-messina-chri.name: Chris Messina
fl-orange-2026-county-mayor-messina-chri.bio: Tech entrepreneur and education philanthropist who founded and ran several medical technology businesses.

positions.stance: Says families deserve tax relief, "not more wasteful spending," and supports Yes on Amendment 3 to reduce the property-tax burden.
Proposes an Orange County Works program to expand vocational, technical, and workforce training connecting residents with trade skills employers need.
Aims to attract high-paying, technology-driven employers and will champion bringing a future Space Force Academy to Central Florida.
Supports "Smarter Growth. Less Sprawl": converting vacant commercial properties into housing and services, and modernizing and right-sizing LYNX.
Seeks to diversify the economy by attracting space technology firms and advanced manufacturers relocating to the United States.

fl-orange-2026-county-mayor-russell-tiff.name: Tiffany Moore Russell
fl-orange-2026-county-mayor-russell-tiff.bio: Orange County Clerk of Courts elected in 2014, former two-term Orange County Commissioner for District 6, and attorney.

positions.stance: Lists "Making Housing More Accessible" as part of her vision for Orange County.
Lists "Ensuring Equitable Development that Prioritize Smart Growth" as part of her vision.
Lists "Enhancing and Investing in Innovative Transportation Solutions" as part of her vision.
Lists "Revitalizing Infrastructure" as part of her vision.
Lists "Investing in Public Safety" as part of her vision.

fl-orange-2026-clerk-of-courts-thomas-te.name: Terrell Thomas
fl-orange-2026-clerk-of-courts-thomas-te.bio: Worked nearly 20 years at the Orange County Clerk of Courts starting in 1998, then in court technology consulting including Tyler Technologies; owner of Dev.G9 Digital.

positions.stance: "People First": will invest in employees, develop leaders, and foster a culture that empowers every team member to deliver exceptional public service.
"Community Focused": will expand outreach, strengthen partnerships, and improve accessibility so residents can easily connect with Clerk services.
"Future Ready": will embrace modern technology, cybersecurity, continuous improvement, and fiscal responsibility while maximizing existing investments.
Says every resident deserves reliable county services, responsibly spent tax dollars, and honest, transparent officials.
Believes government's role "is to protect our rights, not dictate how we live our lives."
Proposes basing property taxes on 1% of purchase price, with annual increases capped at 2% or inflation, whichever is lower.
Supports giving first responders the tools, training, and resources to do their jobs safely and effectively.

il-cook-2026-sheriff-sandefur-brad.name: Brad Sandefur
il-cook-2026-sheriff-sandefur-brad.bio: Cook County Sheriff's Office officer since 1990, including 17 years as a shift commander, and U.S. Marine Corps veteran.

positions.stance: Supports major changes to the SAFE-T Act and Pretrial Fairness Act, with stronger public-safety safeguards and handling of repeat offenders.
Supports mental health diversion when appropriate, expanded residential psychiatric capacity, and longer-term residential drug rehabilitation.
Will prioritize more cross-training, broader arrest-procedure instruction, and stronger preparation for specialized and street assignments.
Supports restructuring the Sheriff's Merit Board and strengthening pre-hire investigations.
Will insist on clear professional expectations and objective disciplinary procedures for sworn staff while protecting due process.

il-cook-2026-assessor-tsatsoulis-nico.name: Nico Tsatsoulis
il-cook-2026-assessor-tsatsoulis-nico.bio: Has worked in finance, retail, wholesale, and real estate; Libertarian Committeeperson for Chicago's 5th Ward.

positions.stance: Wants to "Cap property taxes to 1% of purchase value."
Supports using actual sales values instead of government-derived valuations to determine property assessments.
Supports ending policies that shift a greater property tax burden onto commercial properties.
Supports reforms limiting annual increases in assessed values to keep property taxes stable and predictable.

il-cook-2026-cps-board-president-henders.name: Victor P. Henderson
il-cook-2026-cps-board-president-henders.bio: Attorney and certified public accountant; former president of the Chicago Bar Association and former counsel to the U.S. House Ethics Committee.

positions.stance: "Students Come First - No Exceptions": every hire, contract, and board decision must be made in the context of what is best for students.
Says CPS must re-commit to providing wraparound services that keep kids safe and nourished.
Says CPS needs an open door to parents and community leaders who understand each neighborhood's unique challenges.
Says the board president must rein in unnecessary, politically-driven costs while directing as much funding as possible to the classroom.
Says improving neighborhood public schools is key to attracting and retaining young families in Chicago.

il-cook-2026-cps-board-president-biggs-j.name: Jessica Biggs
il-cook-2026-cps-board-president-biggs-j.bio: Chicago Board of Education member, former principal of Burke Elementary School, and former special education teacher.

positions.stance: "Put Students First — Not Politics": will refocus the board on every child's right to an excellent education regardless of zip code.
Will build district-wide structures bringing LSC leaders, faith institutions, families, and local organizations into the board's ongoing work.
Will convene City and State partners on a multi-year financial recovery plan aiming for an investment-grade credit rating and cash reserves.
Pledges to answer to children, parents, and taxpayers, "not the Mayor, not a union, and not any donor."
